records.text: Corvane Robotics thesis (Mar 11): warehouse picking robots with the best uptime in the category; a 1.9 bn backlog covers two years of revenue. Buy to a 12 percent weight. Conviction: high.

Corvane premise P1: Halvern Logistics keeps rolling Corvane pickers out across its European sites; Halvern is 41 percent of the backlog. The thesis breaks if Halvern builds its own robots or freezes third-party orders.
Corvane premise P2: gross margin stays above 38 percent while the second plant ramps.
Corvane Q2 (Aug 5): revenue up 22 percent, gross margin 39.4 percent, backlog 2.0 bn. Halvern rollout on track: 9 more sites live.

Halvern Logistics capital markets day (Sep 30): from 2027 Halvern will build its warehouse automation and software in-house, freeze new third-party technology contracts, and leave its leased Rotterdam hub when the lease ends in March 2027. For Corvane, about 41 percent of the backlog is at risk.
Corvane conviction cut to medium (Oct 2) after the Halvern news; revisit the position on the Q3 call on Oct 29.
Tessaly Freight Software thesis (Apr 2): the warehouse-management platform that mid-size 3PLs are standardising on; net revenue retention 121 percent. Buy to an 11 percent weight. Conviction: high.

Tessaly premise P1: Halvern Logistics migrates its 60 European warehouses to the Tessaly WMS by mid-2027, about 30 percent of next year's growth. The thesis breaks if Halvern stops buying third-party warehouse software.
Tessaly premise P2: net revenue retention stays above 115 percent.
Tessaly Q2 (Aug 12): net revenue retention 119 percent, ARR up 34 percent; the Halvern migration is on schedule, 14 of 60 sites live.
Tessaly conviction reaffirmed high (Oct 7): Q2 was clean and the Halvern migration is on schedule. Add on weakness.
Brightmoor Logistics REIT thesis (Feb 18): big-box logistics sheds at port gateways, 97 percent occupied, 6.1 percent dividend yield. Hold a 9 percent weight. Conviction: high.
Brightmoor premise P1: anchor tenant Halvern Logistics renews the Rotterdam hub lease in March 2027; the hub is 18 percent of the rent roll. The thesis breaks if Halvern leaves the hub.
Brightmoor premise P2: portfolio occupancy stays above 94 percent.
Brightmoor Q2 (Jul 29): occupancy 97 percent, like-for-like rents up 4 percent; management expects renewal talks with Halvern on the Rotterdam hub to start in Q4.
Brightmoor conviction high (Sep 8): rents rising, the dividend is covered 1.3 times.
Quillon Sensors thesis (Jan 20): lidar-on-chip for factory safety, design wins at four of the five largest robot makers. Buy to a 10 percent weight. Conviction: high.
Quillon premise P1: Feldspar Foundry keeps allocating 28nm capacity to Quillon; Feldspar makes every Quillon chip. The thesis breaks if Feldspar cuts that allocation.
Feldspar Foundry (Sep 17) is adding a second 28nm line in Q1 2027, raising that capacity by about 40 percent; Quillon's allocation is confirmed.
Quillon conviction high (Sep 18): supply worry resolved by the new Feldspar line.
Veridane Motion thesis (May 6): motor-control chips for e-bikes and light EVs, taking share in Europe. Buy to an 8 percent weight. Conviction: medium.
Veridane premise P1: Feldspar Foundry 28nm supply holds through 2027; Feldspar makes 70 percent of Veridane's chips. The thesis breaks if Feldspar cuts that capacity.
Veridane Q2 (Aug 20): revenue up 15 percent, channel inventory normal, full-year guidance kept.
Ostia Payments thesis (Mar 25): payment acceptance for independent clinics, sticky integrations, volume compounding above 25 percent a year. Buy to a 13 percent weight. Conviction: high.
Ostia premise P1: the take rate stays at or above 0.42 percent of volume.
Ostia Q2 (Aug 7): take rate 0.44 percent, payment volume up 27 percent.
Marrowind Energy thesis (Jun 10): offshore wind service contracts with 15-year terms; the 2027 North Sea tender would double the order book. Buy to a 9 percent weight. Conviction: medium.
Marrowind premise P1: the North Sea service tender is awarded on schedule in Q1 2027.
Marrowind (Sep 24): the North Sea tender shortlist is out and Marrowind is on it; the award is still expected in Q1 2027.
